claim: Paraspeckles are nuclear bodies that form around the long non-coding RNA, Neat1, and RNA-binding proteins.
source: Paraspeckles are nuclear bodies form around the long non-coding RNA, Neat1, and RNA-binding proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established background knowledge about paraspeckles.

claim: Paraspeckles control gene expression at a post-transcriptional level by means of nuclear retention of mRNA containing inverted repeats of Alu sequences (IRAlu) in their 3'-UTR.
source: While their role is not fully understood, they are believed to control gene expression at a post-transcriptional level by means of the nuclear retention of mRNA containing in their 3'-UTR inverted repeats of Alu sequences (IRAlu).
evidence: This is stated as a belief based on existing knowledge about paraspeckle function.

claim: All components of paraspeckles including four major proteins and Neat1 displayed a circadian expression pattern in pituitary cells.
source: In this study, we found that, in pituitary cells, all components of paraspeckles including four major proteins and Neat1 displayed a circadian expression pattern.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3.

claim: Insertion of IRAlu at the 3'-UTR of the EGFP cDNA led to a rhythmic circadian nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA.
source: Furthermore the insertion of IRAlu at the 3'-UTR of the EGFP cDNA led to a rhythmic circadian nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA that was lost when paraspeckles were disrupted whereas insertion of a single antisense Alu had only a weak effect.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Rhythmic circadian nuclear retention of egfp mRNA was lost when paraspeckles were disrupted.
source: Furthermore the insertion of IRAlu at the 3'-UTR of the EGFP cDNA led to a rhythmic circadian nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA that was lost when paraspeckles were disrupted whereas insertion of a single antisense Alu had only a weak effect.
evidence: This is supported by loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Insertion of a single antisense Alu had only a weak effect on circadian nuclear retention of egfp mRNA.
source: Furthermore the insertion of IRAlu at the 3'-UTR of the EGFP cDNA led to a rhythmic circadian nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA that was lost when paraspeckles were disrupted whereas insertion of a single antisense Alu had only a weak effect.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data comparing Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines shown in Figure 5A.

claim: IRAlu elements drive a circadian expression of EGFP protein.
source: Using real-time video-microscopy, these IRAlu were further shown to drive a circadian expression of EGFP protein.
evidence: This is supported by real-time video microscopy data shown in Figure 5D and Video 1.

claim: Paraspeckles control circadian gene expression at a post-transcriptional level through their circadian expression.
source: This study shows that paraspeckles, thanks to their circadian expression, control circadian gene expression at a post-transcriptional level.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, supported by multiple experimental findings.

claim: The circadian clock orchestrates daily rhythms in metabolism, physiology and behavior that allow organisms to anticipate regular changes in their environment.
source: The circadian clock orchestrates daily rhythms in metabolism, physiology and behavior that allow organisms to anticipate regular changes in their environment, increasing their adaptation (Asher and Schibler, 2011).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citation to Asher and Schibler, 2011.

claim: Circadian rhythms are underpinned by daily rhythms of gene expression.
source: Circadian rhythms are underpinned by daily rhythms of gene expression.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field of circadian biology.

claim: The transcriptional component of circadian rhythms is well understood.
source: The transcriptional component of these rhythms is well understood (Zhang and Kay, 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Zhang and Kay, 2010.

claim: Post-transcriptional controls are emerging as crucial modulators of circadian clocks.
source: Though the core circadian system has concentrated on transcriptional control, it has been apparent that substantial regulation is achieved after transcription so that post-transcriptional controls are emerging as crucial modulators of circadian clocks (Lim and Allada, 2013; Wang et al., 2013; Menet et al., 2012; Koike et al., 2012; Hurley et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to recent literature.

claim: Approximately 1%-10% of genes are subjected to circadian control directly or indirectly in eukaryotes.
source: While in eukaryotes, approximately 1%-10% genes are subjected to circadian control directly or indirectly only ~1/5 of the mRNAs that display rhythmic expression are directly driven by transcription, which suggests that post-transcriptional mechanisms including RNA splicing, polyadenylation, mRNA stability, mRNA cytoplasmic export and RNAs nuclear retention are essential layers for generation of gene expression rhythmicity (Partch et al., 2014; Menet et al., 2012; Koike et al., 2012; Hurley et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Only approximately 1/5 of the mRNAs that display rhythmic expression are directly driven by transcription.
source: While in eukaryotes, approximately 1%-10% genes are subjected to circadian control directly or indirectly only ~1/5 of the mRNAs that display rhythmic expression are directly driven by transcription, which suggests that post-transcriptional mechanisms including RNA splicing, polyadenylation, mRNA stability, mRNA cytoplasmic export and RNAs nuclear retention are essential layers for generation of gene expression rhythmicity (Partch et al., 2014; Menet et al., 2012; Koike et al., 2012; Hurley et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Post-transcriptional mechanisms including RNA splicing, polyadenylation, mRNA stability, mRNA cytoplasmic export and RNAs nuclear retention are essential layers for generation of gene expression rhythmicity.
source: While in eukaryotes, approximately 1%-10% genes are subjected to circadian control directly or indirectly only ~1/5 of the mRNAs that display rhythmic expression are directly driven by transcription, which suggests that post-transcriptional mechanisms including RNA splicing, polyadenylation, mRNA stability, mRNA cytoplasmic export and RNAs nuclear retention are essential layers for generation of gene expression rhythmicity (Partch et al., 2014; Menet et al., 2012; Koike et al., 2012; Hurley et al., 2014).
evidence: This is inferred from the data cited and represents a conclusion drawn from multiple studies.

claim: Paraspeckles are recently identified nuclear bodies that have been shown to retain RNAs in the nucleus.
source: Paraspeckles are recently identified nuclear bodies that have been shown to retain RNAs in the nucleus.
evidence: This is established knowledge about paraspeckles.

claim: Paraspeckles contain proteins PSPC1, RBM14, NONO, and SFPQ.
source: Paraspeckles contain proteins PSPC1, RBM14, NONO, and SFPQ (Prasanth et al., 2005) and are usually detected as a variable number of discrete dots found in close proximity to nuclear speckles (Bond and Fox, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Prasanth et al., 2005 and Bond and Fox, 2009.

claim: Paraspeckles are usually detected as a variable number of discrete dots found in close proximity to nuclear speckles.
source: Paraspeckles contain proteins PSPC1, RBM14, NONO, and SFPQ (Prasanth et al., 2005) and are usually detected as a variable number of discrete dots found in close proximity to nuclear speckles (Bond and Fox, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Bond and Fox, 2009.

claim: Neat1 is exclusively localized to paraspeckles and serves as a structural component.
source: One long noncoding RNA, nuclear-enriched abundant transcript one (Neat1), exclusively localized to paraspeckles serves as a structural component (Hutchinson et al., 2007; Chen and Carmichael, 2009; Clemson et al., 2009; Sasaki and Hirose, 2009; Sunwoo et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations.

claim: The Neat1 locus generates short and long transcripts from the same promoter, previously identified as MENε (Neat1-1) and MENβ (Neat1-2).
source: The locus generates short and long transcripts from the same promoter, which have previously been identified as MENε (Neat1-1) and MENβ (Neat1-2), respectively (Guru et al., 1997; Sasaki and Hirose, 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Guru et al., 1997 and Sasaki and Hirose, 2009.

claim: Specific depletion of Neat1-2 leads to disruption of paraspeckles.
source: Because specific depletion of Neat1-2 leads to disruption of paraspeckles (Sasaki and Hirose, 2009) Neat1-1 alone cannot induce paraspeckle formation.
evidence: This is supported by citation to Sasaki and Hirose, 2009.

claim: Neat1-1 alone cannot induce paraspeckle formation.
source: Because specific depletion of Neat1-2 leads to disruption of paraspeckles (Sasaki and Hirose, 2009) Neat1-1 alone cannot induce paraspeckle formation.
evidence: This is inferred from the fact that Neat1-2 depletion disrupts paraspeckles.

claim: Paraspeckles retain in the nucleus RNAs containing duplex structures.
source: Paraspeckles have been shown to retain in the nucleus RNAs containing duplex structures (Chen and Carmichael, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen and Carmichael, 2008.

claim: The mouse cationic amino acid transporter 2 (Cat2) transcribed nuclear RNA, Ctn-RNA, is an alternatively spliced form of the Cat2 mRNA that contains a dsRNA structure resulting from inverted short inter-spersed nuclear elements (SINEs) in its 3'-UTR.
source: This is the case for the mouse cationic amino acid transporter 2 (Cat2) transcribed nuclear RNA, Ctn-RNA, an alternatively spliced form of the Cat2 mRNA, which contains a dsRNA structure resulting from inverted short inter-spersed nuclear elements (SINEs) in its 3'-UTR (Prasanth et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Prasanth et al., 2005.

claim: Hundreds of genes in human cells contain inverted repeated SINEs (mainly Alu elements) in their 3'-UTRs.
source: In human cells, hundreds of genes contain inverted repeated SINEs (mainly Alu elements) in their 3'-UTRs.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the human genome.

claim: Alu elements are unique to primates and account for almost all of the human SINEs and >10% of the genome.
source: Alu elements are unique to primates and account for almost all of the human SINEs and >10% of the genome.
evidence: This is established knowledge about Alu elements.

claim: The abundance of Alu elements leads to the frequent occurrence of inverted repeat structures (IRAlus) in gene regions.
source: Their abundance leads to the frequent occurrence of inverted repeat structures (inverted repeated Alu elements [IRAlus]) in gene regions (Chen et al., 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citation to Chen et al., 2008.

claim: mRNAs containing IRAlus in their 3'-UTRs like Nicolin 1 (NICN1) or Lin 28 are retained in the nucleus in paraspeckles.
source: It has been reported previously that mRNAs containing IRAlus in their 3'-UTRs like Nicolin 1 (NICN1) or Lin 28 are retained in the nucleus in paraspeckles (Chen et al., 2008; Chen and Carmichael, 2008).
evidence: This is supported by citations to Chen et al., 2008 and Chen and Carmichael, 2008.

claim: Nuclear retention pathway of IRAlus in 3'-UTRs of genes provides an additional layer of gene regulation by sequestering mature mRNAs within the nucleus.
source: Therefore, this nuclear retention pathway of IRAlus in 3'-UTRs of genes provides an additional layer of gene regulation by sequestering mature mRNAs within the nucleus.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that IRAlus cause nuclear retention.

claim: Two protein components of paraspeckles, NONO and SFPQ, display a circadian expression pattern in primary cultures of pituitary cells and in the GH4C1 rat pituitary cell line.
source: We recently reported that two protein components of paraspeckles, namely NONO and SFPQ, display a circadian expression pattern in primary cultures of pituitary cells as well as in a rat pituitary cell line, the GH4C1 cells (Becquet et al., 2014; Guillaumond et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: SFPQ, NONO, PSPC1 and RBM14 staining appeared as punctate clusters located exclusively within the boundaries of the nucleus in GH4C1 cells.
source: SFPQ (green Figure 1A,C), NONO (green Figure 1B,D), PSPC1 (red Figure 1A,B) and RBM14 (red Figure 1C,D) staining appeared as punctate clusters located exclusively within the boundaries of the nucleus as delimitated by Hoechst labeling (Figure 1A,B,C,D, 4th column).
evidence: This is supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Some punctate clusters of SFPQ or NONO overlap with PSPC1 or RBM14 in subnuclear structures reminiscent of paraspeckles.
source: When SFPQ or NONO staining was merged with PSPC1 (Figure 1A,B, 3rd and 4th columns) on the one hand or RBM14 (Figure 1C,D, 3rd and 4th columns) on the other hand, some punctate clusters were found to overlap with each other in subnuclear structures reminiscent of paraspeckles.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: A 20- to 80-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA was obtained with antibodies against NONO, SFPQ, RBM14 or PSPC1 compared to a non-specific antibody.
source: A 20- to 80-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA was obtained with these antibodies as compared to an irrelevant non-specific antibody (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The four major protein components of paraspeckles bind the structural lncRNA Neat1 in GH4C1 cells.
source: These results showed that the four major protein components of paraspeckles bound the structural lncRNA Neat1, confirming the presence of paraspeckle nuclear bodies in GH4C1 cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the RIP data showing enrichment of Neat1 RNA with paraspeckle protein antibodies.

claim: Neat1 RNA FISH staining appeared as regular punctates within the boundaries of the nucleus under confocal laser scanning microscope.
source: Under confocal laser scanning microscope, Neat1 RNA FISH staining appeared as regular punctates within the boundaries of the nucleus (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The number of Neat1 RNA foci was low and variable from one cell to the other.
source: Number of foci was low and variable from one cell to the other.
evidence: This is an observation from the FISH experiments.

claim: STORM analysis showed that Neat1 labeling of paraspeckle bodies was elliptical rather than round in shape.
source: In addition to the precision in the real size of paraspeckle bodies, super-resolution analysis allowed also to show that Neat1 labeling of paraspeckle bodies was not round in shape, being merely elliptical.
evidence: This is supported by STORM microscopy data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The averaged ratio of Height to Width of paraspeckles was >1 (1.53 ± 0.1) as measured by STORM.
source: Indeed using an imaging software (NIS-Elements, Nikon France S.A, Champigny sur Marne, France) we showed that the averaged ratio of Height to Width (n=10) was >1 (1.53 ± 0.1) and the mean surface area was 24,960 ± 4831 nm2 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of STORM data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The mean surface area of paraspeckles was 24,960 ± 4831 nm2 as measured by STORM.
source: Indeed using an imaging software (NIS-Elements, Nikon France S.A, Champigny sur Marne, France) we showed that the averaged ratio of Height to Width (n=10) was >1 (1.53 ± 0.1) and the mean surface area was 24,960 ± 4831 nm2 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative analysis of STORM data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: RBM14 and PSPC1 proteins displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells over the T2-T30 time period.
source: Indeed, RBM14 and PSPC1 proteins displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells over the T2-T30 time period that could be fitted with a non-linear cosinor fit in which the period value (2pi/Frequency) was constrained to the circadian period value 24 hr (equation values given in Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The rhythmic expression pattern of RBM14 and PSPC1 proteins matched with that of NONO and SFPQ proteins.
source: It may be noticed that the rhythmic expression pattern of RBM14 and PSPC1 proteins (Figure 3A) matched quite correctly with that of NONO and SFPQ proteins we previously reported (see Figure 6A in Guillaumond et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred by comparing current data with previously published data.

claim: Neat1 RNA levels (Neat1-1 + Neat1-2) displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells over the T2-T38 time period.
source: As shown in Figure 3B, Neat1 RNA levels (Neat1-1 + Neat1-2) displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells over the T2-T38 time period (cosinor fit values given in Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Neat1 RNA levels (Neat1-1 + Neat1-2) displayed a circadian expression pattern in several mouse tissues including the pituitary gland, spleen, and adrenal gland.
source: Neat1 RNA levels (Neat1-1 + Neat1-2) also displayed a circadian expression pattern in several mouse tissues including the pituitary gland but also other peripheral oscillators such as the spleen or the adrenal gland (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data from mouse tissues shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Neat1 RNA levels displayed a circadian expression pattern in the suprachiasmatic nuclei.
source: This was also the case in the central clock, namely the suprachiasmatic nuclei (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Binding of NONO, SFPQ, RBM14 and PSPC1 on Neat1 RNA displayed a rhythmic pattern in GH4C1 cells.
source: As shown in Figure 3C, binding of the four paraspeckle-associated proteins on Neat1 RNA displayed a rhythmic pattern (cosinor fit values given in Figure 3—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Maximum binding of the four paraspeckle proteins on Neat1 RNA was reached between 6 and 10 hr after the medium change.
source: Maximum binding on Neat1 RNA was reached between 6 and 10 hr after the medium change for the four proteins (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is observed from the RIP data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: The total number of paraspeckles per well fluctuated over time, being significantly lower 15 hr after the medium change.
source: In cells arrested at four different times after the medium change, the total number of paraspeckles per well was shown to fluctuate, being significantly lower 15 hr after the medium change i.e. at a time when Neat1 RNA levels were around the lowest levels (Figure 3D, F3,103=9.531 p<0.0001).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FISH data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The mean number of paraspeckles per cell reached a minimum value 15 hr after the medium change.
source: Furthermore at this time point, the mean number of paraspeckles per cell reached a minimum value (Figure 3D, F3447= 5.456, p<0.001).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative FISH data shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The rhythm of Neat1 and its associated proteins translates into a rhythm in the number of paraspeckles inside the cells.
source: Taken together, these results showed that the rhythm of Neat1 and its associated proteins reported above translate into a rhythm in the number of paraspeckles inside the cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the combined observations of rhythmic Neat1 expression and rhythmic paraspeckle number.

claim: IRAlu elements derived from NICN1 significantly reduced EGFP expression when compared with the Alu element.
source: In agreement with previous results by Chen et al (Chen and Carmichael, 2008), the IRAlu elements derived from NICN1 significantly reduced EGFP expression when compared with the Alu element (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is supported by fluorescence microscopy and Western blot data shown in Figure 4A-C.

claim: IRAlu elements caused a significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells compared to Alu element.
source: This is here evidenced both by the significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells (Figure 4B) and by the significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to both Alu–egfp cell line (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: IRAlu elements caused a significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to Alu-egfp cell line.
source: This is here evidenced both by the significant reduction in the number of fluorescent cells (Figure 4B) and by the significant decrease in relative EGFP levels measured by western blotting in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to both Alu–egfp cell line (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by Western blot data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: No difference in gene expression was observed between the parent plasmid pEGFP and derivatives that contained a single Alu element.
source: By contrast, we have not observed any difference in gene expression between the parent plasmid pEGFP and derivatives that contained a single Alu element (data not shown).
evidence: This is stated as an observation from experiments, though data is not shown.

claim: IRAlu from Nicn1 caused a more than two-fold greater nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA when compared with the corresponding Alu element.
source: As shown in Figure 4D, the IRAlu from Nicn1 caused a more than two-fold greater nuclear retention of the egfp mRNA when compared with the corresponding Alu element.
evidence: This is supported by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: There is no significant difference in nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution of egfp-Alu mRNA compared with control.
source: On the other hand, there is no significant difference in nuclear/cytoplasmic distribution of egfp-Alu mRNA compared with control (data not shown), consistent with our finding that a single Alu element in the 3'-UTR does not affect EGFP gene expression.
evidence: This is stated as an observation, though data is not shown.

claim: Nuclear retention of IRAlu-containing egfp mRNA correlates with silencing of EGFP protein expression.
source: It then appears that nuclear retention of IRAlu-containing egfp mRNA correlates with silencing of EGFP protein expression (Figure 4A–C).
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between nuclear retention data and protein expression data.

claim: PSPC1 protein was associated with IRAlu-egfp mRNA but not with Alu-egfp mRNA.
source: While the enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in the two cell lines (Figure 4E), enrichment in egfp mRNA was significant only in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F), attesting that PSPC1 protein was associated to IRAlu-egfp and not to Alu-egfp mRNA.
evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: The enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines.
source: While the enrichment in lncRNA Neat1 obtained after use of PSPC1 antibody was comparable in the two cell lines (Figure 4E), enrichment in egfp mRNA was significant only in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F), attesting that PSPC1 protein was associated to IRAlu-egfp and not to Alu-egfp mRNA.
evidence: This is supported by RIP experimental data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Two anti-sense oligonucleotides allowed a 30 to 40-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA compared to Neat1 RNA input from cross-linked GH4C1 cellular extracts.
source: With this strategy, we found that two anti-sense oligonucleotides allowed a 30 to 40-fold enrichment in Neat1 RNA compared to Neat1 RNA input from cross-linked GH4C1 cellular extracts (Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: The enrichment in Neat1 was not statistically different in Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines after Neat1 RNA pull-down.
source: While one of the specific oligonucleotide (S oligo 2) is more efficient than the other (S oligo 1) to pull-down Neat1, the enrichment in Neat1 was not statistically different in the two Alu-egfp and IRAlu-egfp cell lines (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The amounts of egfp mRNA retrieved after Neat1 RNA pull-down were significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp compared to Alu-egfp cell line.
source: By contrast, the amounts of egfp mRNA retrieved after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe were significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp compared to Alu-egfp cell line (Figure 4F).
evidence: This is supported by RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: IRAlu-egfp mRNA was preferentially associated with Neat1-containing paraspeckles compared to Alu-egfp mRNA.
source: This result clearly showed that IRAlu-egfp mRNA was preferentially associated with Neat1-containing paraspeckles compared to Alu-egfp mRNA.
evidence: This is inferred from the RNA pull-down data showing higher enrichment of IRAlu-egfp mRNA with Neat1.

claim: High amplitude circadian variations in the nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of egfp mRNA were observed in IRAlu-egfp cell line.
source: We showed that in addition to the previously described higher ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to Alu-egfp cell lines (Figure 4D) we also found high amplitude circadian variations in this ratio in IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is supported by time-course nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: The magnitude of the rhythmic pattern of nuclear/cytoplasmic egfp mRNA ratio was highly reduced in Alu-egfp cell line compared to IRAlu-egfp cell line.
source: Whereas it was observed that the nuclear/cytoplasmic ratio of egfp mRNA could also be fitted by a cosinor equation in Alu-egfp cell line, the magnitude of this rhythmic pattern was highly reduced (Figure 5A) as compared to IRAlu-egfp cell line (Figure 5—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of cosinor fit parameters shown in Figure 5A and Figure 5—source data 1.

claim: Neat1 RNA levels were reduced to around 60% after treatment with specific siRNA compared to negative control siRNA in IRAlu-egfp cell line.
source: Neat1 has been previously shown by others to be effectively knocked down by siRNA (Chen and Carmichael, 2009; Clemson et al., 2009), and we indeed verified by RT-qPCR that Neat1 RNA levels were reduced in IRAlu-egfp cell line to around 60% after treatment with specific siRNA compared to negative control siRNA, a decrease that was comparable to that obtained with Neat1 ASO (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A)
evidence: This is supported by RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Neat1 rhythmic expression pattern was suppressed by both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO.
source: more importantly, whereas Neat1 rhythmic expression pattern was not affected by negative control (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), it was suppressed both by Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D).
evidence: This is supported by time-course RT-qPCR data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1C,D.

claim: The relative ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA levels was significantly decreased when IRAlu-egfp cells were transfected with Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO compared to negative control.
source: In addition, when IRAlu-egfp cells were transfected either by Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO as compared to negative control, the relative ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic egfp mRNA levels was significantly decreased (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is supported by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Circadian egfp mRNA nuclear retention was abolished after both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO transfection.
source: Moreover, whereas the circadian egfp mRNA nuclear retention was not affected after transfection of the cells by the negative control (not shown), it was abolished after both Neat1 siRNA and Neat1 ASO transfection (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is supported by time-course data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: The IRAlu-egfp reporter does not cycle when paraspeckles are disrupted.
source: These loss of function experiments showed that the IRAlu-egfp reporter does not cycle when paraspeckles are disrupted.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of rhythmic nuclear retention after Neat1 knockdown.

claim: The percent of cells that could be fitted by cosinor equation with a R2>0.5 was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines.
source: The percent of cells that could be fitted by cosinor equation with a R2>0.5 was then calculated for each cell line. This percent was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines (Figure 5D) allowing to show that insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
evidence: This is supported by real-time video microscopy data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: Insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
source: This percent was significantly higher in IRAlu-egfp cell line compared to the Alu-egfp and egfp cell lines (Figure 5D) allowing to show that insertion of an IRAlu element in the 3'-UTR of egfp mRNA promoted EGFP protein circadian expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the higher percentage of rhythmic cells in IRAlu-egfp cell line.

claim: 4268 genes (28% of expressed transcripts in GH4C1 cells) were common to the lists obtained with the two specific oligonucleotides used for Neat1 RNA pull-down.
source: We assessed the specificity of Neat 1 RNA pull-down by crossing the FPKM>1-limited lists obtained with the two specific oligonucleotides. 4268 genes (28% of expressed transcripts in GH4C1 cells) were common to the two lists (Figure 6—source data 1).
evidence: This is supported by RNA sequencing data analysis.

claim: The 4268 common genes represented 65% of the list obtained with S oligo 1 and 83% of the list obtained with S oligo 2.
source: This represented 65% of the list obtained with S oligo 1 and 83% of the list obtained with S oligo 2.
evidence: This is calculated from the RNA sequencing data.

claim: 68 genes out of 362 from the list of pituitary circadian transcripts (18.8%) were found to be included in the Neat1 RNA targets dataset.
source: We first compared the mouse pituitary circadian transcriptome previously published (Hughes et al., 2007) with our data set of Neat1 RNA targets. It appeared that 68 genes out of 362 from the list of pituitary circadian transcripts (18.8% ) were found to be included in our data set (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claim: 182 genes out of 675 from the list of post-transcriptional circadian genes in the liver (27%) were found to be included in the Neat1 RNA targets dataset.
source: To this end, we compared the list of putative post-transcriptional cycling transcripts established by Menet et al. (Menet et al., 2012) in the mouse liver with our list of Neat1 RNA targets. Although these two lists have been established in two different tissues from two different species, it appeared that 182 genes out of 675 from the list of post-transcriptional circadian genes in the liver (27%) were found to be included in our data set (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Very few genes (24 genes) were common to the list of Hughes et al. and that of Menet et al.
source: In agreement with the assumption that rhythmic circadian genes are tissue specific, we found very few genes (24 genes) common to the list of Hughes et al. (<7%) (Hughes et al., 2007) and that of Menet et al. (<4%) (Menet et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of the two published datasets.

claim: 6 genes out of 24 common genes (25%) between Hughes et al. and Menet et al. lists were Neat1 RNA targets.
source: In spite of this reduced overlap, we found that 6 genes out of these 24 common genes (25% ) were Neat1 RNA targets (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is supported by comparison of datasets shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Seven selected genes (Calr, Evi5, Maged1, Canx, Pcbp2, Syne1, and Fkbp4) were significantly enriched after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe.
source: First we verified by qPCR the specific association of the seven selected genes with Neat1. To this end, we determined the enrichment in these seven mRNA obtained after Neat1 RNA pull-down with the two specific biotinylated complementary oligonucleotides that target Neat1 compared to the biotinylated irrelevant probe. As shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1, the seven selected genes were significantly enriched after Neat1 RNA pull-down by the two specific probes compared to the non-specific probe.
evidence: This is supported by qPCR validation data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1.

claim: Seven selected genes displayed a rhythmic pattern of nuclear retention in IRAlu-egfp cells.
source: We further found that the seven selected genes displayed a rhythmic pattern of nuclear retention in IRAlu-egfp cells since values obtained for their relative mRNA ratio between nucleoplasm and cytoplasm over the time can be fitted by a sine wave curve with a R squared >0.55 (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 2, Figure 6—source data 2).
evidence: This is supported by time-course nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: The minimum value of the relative ratio nuclear/cytoplasmic mRNA of the seven selected genes occurred roughly 20 hr after the medium change.
source: It may be noticed that the minimum value of the relative ratio nuclear / cytoplasmic mRNA occurred roughly 20 hr after the medium change, i.e. at a time when the levels of paraspeckle protein components and Neat1 RNA were the lowest (Figure 3).
evidence: This is observed from the time-course data and correlated with paraspeckle component levels.

claim: Knockdown of Neat1 RNA by Neat1 siRNA or Neat1 ASO disrupted the circadian pattern of the ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic levels of the seven selected mRNA.
source: In Figure 6C–D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2, it was shown that knockdown of Neat1 RNA, either by Neat1 siRNA (Figure 6C) or by Neat1 ASO (Figure 6D) disrupted the circadian pattern of the ratio of nuclear versus cytoplasmic levels of the seven selected mRNA as assessed by the inability to fit the values obtained with a sine wave curve with a R squared >0.55.
evidence: This is supported by loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 6C-D and Figure 6—figure supplement 2.

claim: Paraspeckles play a role in the rhythmic expression of the seven selected genes.
source: These results showed that paraspeckles play a role in the rhythmic expression of theses selected genes.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss of rhythmic nuclear retention after paraspeckle disruption.

claim: Paraspeckles are found in almost all cultured cell lines and primary cultures from tissues, except for embryonic stem cells.
source: Paraspeckles are found in almost all of the cultured cell lines and primary cultures from tissues (Bond and Fox, 2009), except for embryonic stem cells (Chen and Carmichael, 2009).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Four RNA-binding proteins (NONO, PSPC1, SFPQ, and RBM14) are classified as 'classical' paraspeckle protein components.
source: Four RNA-binding proteins, including three members of the Drosophila melanogaster behavior human splicing (DBHS) family proteins (NONO, PSPC1 and SFPQ) and RNA-binding motif protein 14 (RBM14) are classified as 'classical' paraspeckle protein components (Bond and Fox, 2009; Prasanth et al., 2005; Fox et al., 2002; Nakagawa and Hirose, 2012).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Both endogenous and tagged forms of paraspeckle proteins are found localized within the nucleoplasm as well as paraspeckles in mammalian cells.
source: Both endogenous and tagged forms of these proteins are found localized within the nucleoplasm as well as paraspeckles in mammalian cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge about paraspeckle protein localization.

claim: All four paraspeckle protein components are distributed both in the nucleoplasm and in subnuclear foci in rat pituitary cell line.
source: With a confocal fluorescent study, we report in a rat pituitary cell line that all four paraspeckle protein components are distributed both in the nucleoplasm and in subnuclear foci.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy data shown in Figure 1.

claim: Paraspeckles are small, irregularly sized and unevenly distributed subnuclear bodies in rat pituitary cell nuclei.
source: This allows not only to provide evidence for the existence of paraspeckles in rat pituitary cell nuclei but also to show that as already reported in other cell types, paraspeckles are small, irregularly sized and unevenly distributed subnuclear bodies.
evidence: This is observed from immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1.

claim: When identified by a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and confocal microscopy, paraspeckles appear as round foci in rat pituitary cells.
source: Confirming previous reports in other cell types, when identified by a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and confocal microscopy, paraspeckles appear as round foci in rat pituitary cells.
evidence: This is supported by FISH data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: The diameter of round paraspeckle foci is in the range of around 360 nm.
source: The diameter of such round foci is in the range of that estimated in previous studies (around 360 nm).
evidence: This is compared with previous literature estimates.

claim: After use of a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and STORM analysis, paraspeckles appear as oblong structures with smaller dimensions reminiscent of the interchromatin granule-associated zone (IGAZ).
source: However after use of a combination of Neat1 RNA FISH and STORM analysis, paraspeckles appear more likely as oblong structures with smaller dimensions reminiscent of the interchromatin granule-associated zone (IGAZ) that had been observed under electron microscope and had been reported to correspond to paraspeckles (Cardinale et al., 2007; Bond and Fox, 2009; Souquere et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by STORM data shown in Figure 2C and compared with previous literature.

claim: Width and height measurements obtained after STORM analysis of Neat1 RNA FISH staining are smaller than the dimensions of IGAZ nuclear bodies established by electron microscopy analysis in human and mouse cells.
source: Width and height measurements obtained after STORM analysis of Neat1 RNA FISH staining are smaller than the dimensions of IGAZ nuclear bodies established by an electron microscopy analysis in human and mouse cells (Souquere et al., 2010) suggesting that either IGAZ/paraspeckle nuclear bodies are smaller in rat than in mouse cells or alternatively and more likely, Neat1 RNA staining does not fill in all the nuclear bodies as already proposed (Souquere et al., 2010).
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of STORM measurements with published electron microscopy data.

claim: The circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA in several mouse tissues reflects variations in paraspeckle number.
source: It may then be assumed that the circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA described here in a number of mouse tissue also reflects variations in paraspeckle number although it cannot be excluded that paraspeckle size could also oscillate over the circadian period both in pituitary cells and in other oscillators.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation in GH4C1 cells that Neat1 levels correlate with paraspeckle number.

claim: Paraspeckle size could oscillate over the circadian period in pituitary cells and other oscillators.
source: It may then be assumed that the circadian expression pattern of Neat1 RNA described here in a number of mouse tissue also reflects variations in paraspeckle number although it cannot be excluded that paraspeckle size could also oscillate over the circadian period both in pituitary cells and in other oscillators.
evidence: This is acknowledged as a possibility that cannot be excluded.

claim: A pair of IRAlus in the 3'-UTR of egfp can strongly silence EGFP expression in GH4C1 pituitary cell line.
source: As previously reported by Chen and Carmichael (Chen et al., 2008), we found that a pair of IRAlus in the 3'-UTR of egfp can strongly silence EGFP expression in GH4C1 pituitary cell line and after fractionating cytoplasmic and nuclear RNAs from our two cell lines, we observed that IRAlus-containing egfp mRNA appear to be preferentially retained in the nucleus in comparison with those having a single Alu element.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 4 and confirmed by citation.

claim: IRAlus-containing egfp mRNA appear to be preferentially retained in the nucleus in comparison with those having a single Alu element.
source: As previously reported by Chen and Carmichael (Chen et al., 2008), we found that a pair of IRAlus in the 3'-UTR of egfp can strongly silence EGFP expression in GH4C1 pituitary cell line and after fractionating cytoplasmic and nuclear RNAs from our two cell lines, we observed that IRAlus-containing egfp mRNA appear to be preferentially retained in the nucleus in comparison with those having a single Alu element.
evidence: This is supported by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Silencing EGFP expression mechanism relied on egfp mRNA nuclear retention.
source: It then appeared that silencing EGFP expression mechanism relied on egfp mRNA nuclear retention.
evidence: This is inferred from the correlation between nuclear retention and reduced protein expression.

claim: PSPC1, NONO and SFPQ accumulate in paraspeckles but are also found elsewhere throughout the nucleoplasm and may have functions apart from paraspeckle retention.
source: While PSPC1 as well as NONO and SFPQ accumulate in paraspeckles, these proteins are also found elsewhere throughout the nucleoplasm and thus may have functions apart from paraspeckle retention.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the multifunctional nature of these proteins.

claim: NEAT1 may have only one function in contrast to paraspeckle-associated proteins that are multifunctional.
source: In contrast to paraspeckle-associated proteins that are multifunctional, NEAT1 may have only one function.
evidence: This is stated as a contrast to the multifunctional proteins.

claim: The association of IRAlu egfp mRNA with Neat1 provides convincing evidence for nuclear retention of IRAlu egfp mRNA by paraspeckles.
source: We then developed a technique to characterize nuclear mRNA Neat1 targets using a Neat1 RNA pull-down approach that allowed us to show the association of IRAlu egfp mRNA with Neat1 providing a much more convincing evidence for a nuclear retention of IRAlu egfp mRNA by paraspeckles.
evidence: This is inferred from the Neat1 RNA pull-down data shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Some RNA-binding proteins that target antisense Alu elements within the 3'-UTR of mRNAs display a rhythmic expression pattern.
source: Since antisens Alu elements within the 3'-UTR of mRNAs can be the target of several RNA-binding proteins (Kelley et al., 2014; Zarnack et al., 2013) it may be speculated that some of these RNA-binding proteins display a rhythmic expression pattern accounting for the weak EGFP circadian expression observed in Alu-egfp cell line.
evidence: This is speculated to explain the weak circadian expression in Alu-egfp cells.

claim: HNRNPC displays a circadian expression pattern in several tissues including the mouse pituitary.
source: Among the identified RNA-binding proteins that target antisens Alu elements within the 3'-UTR of mRNAs, HNRNPC was shown to display a circadian expression pattern in several tissues including the mouse pituitary (see CIRCA: http://circadb.hogeneschlab.org/).
evidence: This is supported by reference to the CIRCA database.

claim: HNRNPU and STAUFEN 1 (STAU1) do not display a circadian expression pattern in GH4C1 cells.
source: This is not the case for HNRNPU and STAUFEN 1 (STAU1)-mediated messenger RNA decay we did not find to display a circadian expression pattern in GH4C1 cells (Guillaumond et al., 2011) and (data not shown) and are then unlikely involved in circadian EGFP expression in Alu-egfp cell line.
evidence: This is supported by previous data and unpublished observations.

claim: HNRNPU and STAU1 are unlikely involved in circadian EGFP expression in Alu-egfp cell line.
source: This is not the case for HNRNPU and STAUFEN 1 (STAU1)-mediated messenger RNA decay we did not find to display a circadian expression pattern in GH4C1 cells (Guillaumond et al., 2011) and (data not shown) and are then unlikely involved in circadian EGFP expression in Alu-egfp cell line.
evidence: This is inferred from the lack of circadian expression of these proteins.

claim: The mechanism involved in the circadian nuclear retention of Alu-containing egfp mRNA remains to be determined.
source: The mechanism involved in the circadian nuclear retention of Alu-containing egfp mRNA remains anyway to be determined.
evidence: This acknowledges that the mechanism is not yet understood.

claim: Nuclear retention of the reporter gene by paraspeckles contributes to cycling.
source: Nuclear retention of egfp mRNA in IRAlu-egfp cells is no more cycling when paraspeckles were disrupted assuming that the nuclear retention of the reporter gene by paraspeckles contributes to cycling.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Paraspeckle retention plays a relevant role in circadian gene expression.
source: Furthermore, on a few circadian genes common to either of these lists or both, we showed a loss of rhythmic pattern when paraspeckles were disrupted assuming that paraspeckle retention plays a relevant role in circadian gene expression.
evidence: This is inferred from the loss-of-function experiments shown in Figure 6C-D.

claim: Post-transcriptional circadian regulation plays a major role in determining oscillations at the mRNA level.
source: It is now widely admitted that post-transcriptional circadian regulation plays a major role in determining oscillations at the mRNA level.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Circadian mRNA oscillations could be post-transcriptionally controlled through rhythmic nuclear retention by paraspeckle nuclear bodies.
source: In agreement with this view, the new mechanism described here suggests that circadian mRNA oscillations could be post-transcriptionally controlled through rhythmic nuclear retention by paraspeckle nuclear bodies.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the study, inferred from all the experimental findings.

claim: GH4C1 cells were obtained in 2012 from ATCC and were confirmed to be free of mycoplasma.
source: GH4C1 cells, a rat pituitary somatolactotroph line, were obtained in 2012 from ATCC (CCL-82.2, lot number: 58945448, Molsheim, France) with certificate analysis and were confirmed to be free of mycoplasma (MycoAlert, Lonza, Levallois-Perret, France).
evidence: This is a methodological statement about cell line authentication.
